answer: The ember test I would run is Bond posted as liquidity in a stable pool: a stake earning fees while it sits locked, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a stake earning fees while it sits locked — so privacy survives, and the sable is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the knoll of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
